name: Severe Combined Immunodeficiency due to FOXN1 Deficiency

criteria.description: Congenital athymia or severely hypoplastic thymus on imaging or biopsy
Profound T-cell lymphopenia with low or absent circulating T cells
Identification of pathogenic biallelic mutations in the FOXN1 gene
Congenital alopecia and nail dystrophy as supportive clinical features
Absent or severely reduced T-cell proliferative responses to mitogens

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of severe T-cell immunodeficiency with absent or hypoplastic thymus and biallelic pathogenic FOXN1 mutations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be supported by clinical features such as congenital alopecia and nail dystrophy.

laboratory: Profound T-cell lymphopenia with normal or elevated B and NK cells
Absent T-cell proliferative response to mitogens
imaging: Absent or hypoplastic thymus on chest X-ray or CT scan
other: Congenital alopecia and nail dystrophy on physical examination

distinguishingFeatures: No congenital alopecia or nail dystrophy
22q11.2 deletion detected by FISH or microarray
Thymic aplasia similar but with distinct genetic cause

redFlags: Absent or severely hypoplastic thymus on imaging
references: Pignata C, et al. FOXN1 deficiency: clinical, immunological, and molecular features. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2013.
Ferre EMN, et al. Biallelic mutations in FOXN1 cause severe combined immunodeficiency with congenital alopecia. Nat Genet. 2011.
Orphanet: Severe combined immunodeficiency due to FOXN1 deficiency (ORPHA:169095)
